answer: Each identity must lock bonded collateral, so splitting control does not create free voting power. When evidence links k identities to coordinated equivocation, the pairwise penalty grows as O(k²), while detection applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss; asymmetric depreciation can further reduce recoverable value. An ocean of keys offers no safe harbor: the delta in expected loss makes correlated Sybil control increasingly costly.
